blocks.text:
binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, supply-chain, dep-audit]
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || fail "changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || fail "supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || fail "dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          # The remaining legs are path-gated: success or skipped is fine,
          # anything else fails.
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
              fail "a leg is $r ($name)"
            fi
          done
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      (github.event.inputs.pr != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, mirroring the pinned factory's own block
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write). A reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the caller, so the
# caller must grant at least what the callee declares — an explicit
# read-only block here made every call fail validation with
# startup_failure (live bisect, 2026-09-18); this mirror is the minimal
# consistent set (SEC-08, #796).
permissions:
  contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
  issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
  actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
    # The workflow-level mirror scopes exist for the pinned factory call
    # (a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller); the gate
    # must not inherit them (SEC-08 review, #796).
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 849
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/849
- **Title**: feat(ci): SHA-pinned actions + pin-freshness automation (#796)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-796` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 20
- **Additions**: +520
- **Deletions**: -232
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T20:31:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-23T00:57:20Z

## PR Description

Supersedes #801 (owner-closed unmerged over a merge conflict; reopen refused for non-owner). Same branch `ai/gh-796`, now rebased onto main @ 10715955 (carries #846 runner split, #847 factory pin 54e86fd, #848 SM-gate-bridge). Closes #796 (SEC-08, HIGH).

## What
1. **Every third-party Actions ref in `.github/workflows/*.yml` + composite actions is a full 40-hex commit SHA** (213 refs, 13 distinct actions; SHAs resolved via the GitHub API at pin time). First-party repo-relative refs stay exempt. The factory `uses:` lines (machine-sm.yml, ai-teammate.yml, machine-merge.yml) keep main's current pins (54e86fd) — only the surrounding permissions blocks were added.
2. **Every workflow declares an explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` block** (caller⇄reusable consistent). The ai-teammate mirror is exactly the pinned factory's declared scopes (contents/issues/pull-requests/actions = write — an explicit read-only caller block startup_failure'd the reusable call; live bisect 2026-09-18). The read-only `gate` job narrows further to `contents: read`.
3. **Dual-graph dependency audit**: `dep-audit` matrix [hosted, vendored] — hosted = `pubspec.yaml` alone (what pub.dev consumers resolve), vendored = + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` (CI/release). The split is asserted from the resolved `pubspec.lock` (dart_tui `source: hosted` vs `source: path`), anchored to the entry block boundary, and documented in each leg's job summary.
4. **Supply-chain gate on every PR** (no path gating): AC1 pin-check script (`scripts/check_action_pins.sh` — refs must match `\^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$`; composite actions scanned depth-unlimited, both extensions), AC2 permissions lint (*.yml + *.yaml), AC4 fixture REG (@v4, 40-char non-hex, unpinned nested composite all REJECTED; SHA-pinned accepted).
5. **Quality gate hardening**: a failed/skipped `changes` classifier FAILS the aggregate, and the security legs (supply-chain, dep-audit) must EXECUTE and pass — `skipped` is a dodge, not a pass. Path-gated legs keep success|skipped semantics.
6. **Pin freshness (contract)**: `.github/dependabot.yml` — github-actions ecosystem, weekly, grouped into one PR; Dependabot bumps SHA-pinned refs and their `# vX` comments.

## Coexistence with #848
#848 exempts `chore:pin` PRs from the SM gate bridge; this PR's pin checker still runs on every other PR and over #848's own content (verified: scan passes on the merged tree).

## Verification
- All workflow YAMLs parse; pin scan + AC2 lint green locally and in CI (run 35771469033 on the pre-rebase head: Supply-chain gate + both dep-audit legs success; re-dispatching on this head).
- Fixture REG matrix verified locally (7 scenarios incl. classifier-failed and skipped-security).
- ruby/setup-ruby pinned at the v1.99.0 release-tag commit `e5517072e87f198d9533967ae13d97c11b604005` (ls-remote verified), 7 call sites in lockstep.

## Notes
- Dependabot's first weekly run will open the grouped bump PR; the supply-chain gate re-verifies every ref on it.
- #814 (SEC-07 installer) stacks on this branch and will be re-synced on top of this head.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

---
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full

+# SEC-08 (#796): pin freshness. Dependabot tracks SHA-pinned GitHub Actions
+# refs (it bumps both the ref and the `# vX` comment) across
+# .github/workflows and .github/actions, so pinned SHAs stay current
+# instead of silently rotting. All bumps land as ONE grouped weekly PR —
+# each bump is an independent supply-chain decision, but batching keeps
+# review noise down; the supply-chain gate re-verifies every ref on that
+# PR regardless.
+version: 2
+updates:
+  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
+    directory: /
+    schedule:
+      interval: weekly
+    groups:
+      github-actions:
+        patterns:
+          - "*"

blocks.text:
I've now read the entire diff. Let me now review the full content of the changed files (not just diff). Key files to deep-read:

1. `scripts/check_action_pins.sh` (new, 76 lines) — full content seen in diff.
2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — need to see full content around the new jobs and the quality gate.
3. `.github/dependabot.yml` — full content seen.
4. Other workflows — pins changed.

Let me analyze potential issues:

### check_action_pins.sh analysis

```bash
set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
```

Observations:

1. **Local `action.yml` composite actions in the default mode**: In repo mode, `dir=".github/workflows"`, so it scans `.github/workflows/*.yml` + every `action.yml`/`action.yaml` found under `.github/workflows` at any depth (via find). Wait — the find is `find "$dir" ...`, i.e. under `.github/workflows` only! So composite actions living in `.github/actions/` or elsewhere in the repo (e.g. `.github/actions/*/action.yml`) would NOT be scanned in the default repo mode, because find only scans `$dir` = `.github/workflows`. Hmm wait, let me re-check: the comment says "plus EVERY composite action manifest at any depth". But `find "$dir"` with dir=.github/workflows only descends into .github/workflows. In the repo layout, are there composite actions? Let me check if the repo has `.github/actions/` or `.github/actions/*/action.yml` etc. Actually the fixture mode with `--path tmp/bad-composite` — dir=tmp/bad-composite, and find under it finds `.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml`. In repo mode, the scan would only find action.yml files *under .github/workflows*, NOT under `.github/actions/`.

Wait — but the PR description says "composite actions scanned depth-unlimited, both extensions". The claim: "Every third-party Actions ref in `.github/workflows/*.yml` + composite actions is a full 40-hex commit SHA (213 refs...)". If the repo has composite actions under `.github/actions/` or elsewhere (e.g., `.github/actions/foo/action.yml`), the repo-mode scan misses them. Need to check whether the repo actually has composite actions outside `.github/workflows`.

Let me check: `find .github -name 'action.y*ml'`. If there are composite actions under `.github/actions/`, this is a real gap — the AC1 gate would not scan them even though the PR claims depth-unlimited coverage. That's a potential BLOCKING or IMPORTANT finding (security gate blind spot).

Hmm, but wait — the glob also has `"$dir"/*.yml` — in repo mode that's `.github/workflows/*.yml` again? No: `"$dir"/*.yml` = `.github/workflows/*.yml` — same as the first glob. So in repo mode, globs 1 and 3 are identical, and globs 2 and 4 identical (yaml). Duplicate scanning — harmless but redundant. Actually not a bug, just redundancy.

2. **Duplicate file scanning**: In repo mode, `$dir/.github/workflows/*.yml` and `$dir/*.yml` are the same set (both = `.github/workflows/*.yml`). Each file would be scanned twice, so violations counted twice. Cosmetic.

In fixture mode (`--path tmp/good` where tmp/good has good.yml), globs: `tmp/good/.github/workflows/*.yml` (nullglob → empty) and `tmp/good/*.yml` → good.yml. Fine.

But wait, the AC4 fixture `good-composite` dir: `tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml` — glob finds nothing, finds the action.yaml. Good.

3. **`files+=` with `set -u` and empty arrays**: With `set -u` (nounset), referencing an empty array ("${files[@]}") in old bash (4.2 and earlier) errors; bash 4.4+ is fine. GitHub runners have bash 5. Also `files=()` never happens since nullglob. And if no regular workflows exist but composite actions exist, `files=("${empty}"...)` then appended — `${files[@]}` with nullglob-expansion in assignment: `files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml ...)` — if all four globs are null, files=() — empty array assignment is fine; then `files+=("$f")` fills it. `${#files[@]}` on empty array with set -u: bash 4.4+ OK. ubuntu-latest has bash 5.x. Fine.

4. **grep pattern**: `grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file"` — line-anchored. Multiline `uses:` values (e.g., `uses: >-` folded scalar) wouldn't be caught. Uncommon. Also `uses:` with value starting with `*` (YAML alias) — edge case, not relevant.

Note: `grep -hoE ... | sed ...` — the `|| true` guards grep exit 1 (no matches). With `set -eu` and pipefail? pipefail is NOT set (`set -eu` only), so grep's exit 1 wouldn't kill it anyway; `|| true` extra safety. OK.

5. **What about `uses:` inside comments or strings** — line-anchored `uses:` — a comment line `# uses: actions/checkout@v4`? grep `^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:` — `# uses:` doesn't match because `#` isn't space or dash. Good. A run: scalar with `- uses:` at line start matches... in the string-safe fixture, the run block lines are indented printf strings, e.g. `          printf 'jobs:...- uses: actions/checkout@v4...'` — the line starts with spaces then `printf`, not `uses:`. Good, they tested that.

6. **sha extraction**: `sha="${ref##*@}"` — for a ref with no `@`, e.g. `uses: docker://alpine` handled separately. But what about `uses: ./local` (no ./ prefix, e.g. `uses: ./.github/actions/foo`) — starts with `./` exempt. What about first-party actions referenced as `owner/repo` form? There are none first-party. What about local composite actions referenced relative without `./`? Not valid GitHub syntax — must be `./path`. OK.

Edge: `uses: actions/checkout@` (trailing @, empty sha) → sha="" → fails regex → violation flagged. Good.

Edge: `docker://` image with tag but no digest → flagged. Good. But is `docker://` even used in this repo's workflows? Maybe not; fine.

7. **actionlint-style quoting**: `echo "::error file=$file::..."` — `$file` may contain spaces; fine for GH annotations.

8. **`find` with `-name .git -prune`** — for fixture dirs; ok.

9. **Missing: reusable workflow local refs `uses: ./.github/workflows/x.yml`** — starts with `./` — exempt. Good.

10. **AC2 check in ci.yml**: `grep -q '^permissions:' "$f"` — requires top-level (column 0) `permissions:`. But note: a workflow with ONLY job-level permissions and a top-level `permissions:` appearing nowhere — flagged. In the repo, do all workflows now have top-level permissions? The PR added top-level blocks to ai-teammate, browser-ext, build-macos, ci, nightly, office-addin. Other workflows (bench.yml, bench-4.0.yml, daily-publish.yml, pages.yml, publish-fa-llm.yml, release-appstore.yml, shard-rebalance.yml, site-mobile.yml, store-metadata.yml, build-mobile.yml, aab-gate-selftest.yml, coverage-gardener.yml) — did they have top-level permissions already on main? Need to verify all files in `.github/workflows/` on the PR head have top-level `permissions:`. Let me check the actual files.

Also the AC2 grep would also match a *job-level* `permissions:` if it's at column 0? YAML requires job-level mappings indented, so top-level is column 0. A file where `permissions:` appears at column 0 only within a job... not valid YAML structure (jobs are indented under `jobs:`), so column-0 `permissions:` implies top-level. Good heuristic. But `grep -q '^permissions:'` also matches a line inside a `run: |` block at column 0 — impossible inside block scalars (they're indented). Actually block scalar content is indented, so fine.

11. **dependabot.yml**: `directory: /` — for github-actions ecosystem, "/" covers the whole repo (workflows + composite actions in `.github/`). Good. Weekly grouped. Note: Dependabot ignores `pubspec_overrides`... not relevant. One nuance: `groups.github-actions.patterns: ["*"]` — groups all updates into one PR. Fine.

But: Dependabot's version comments. Dependabot updates `# vX` comments? Actually Dependabot does NOT update trailing comments automatically. Hmm — Dependabot bumps the ref (SHA) when pinning is used... For SHA-pinned actions, Dependabot updates the SHA and... I recall Dependabot does update the comment when it's the conventional `@<sha> # <tag>` format. Actually yes …

name: 'Setup Flutter (persistent self-hosted SDK)'
description: >-
  Marker-pinned Flutter SDK kept under $HOME/actions-runner-yoloit across
  runs. On a persistent self-hosted runner the subosito/flutter-action
  cache is an anti-optimization (issue #354): setup untars a ~1GB archive
  every job and the POST step re-tars the whole SDK every run even when
  the version did not change — 14.5 of 19.7 minutes around a 4-minute
  iOS build. This action downloads the SDK exactly once per pinned
  version and reuses it subsecond afterwards. The SDK lives in
  per-version directories with an atomically-flipped `current` symlink
  (#357 review): both build-macos matrix arch legs run CONCURRENTLY on
  the one self-hosted runner, so every slot mutation is a single
  rename(2) and concurrent installs of the same pin converge instead of
  racing (sdk_slot.py documents the contract; test/
  setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart pins the decision scenarios and
  the regression guard).

inputs:
  flutter-version:
    description: 'Version spec — wildcard (3.47.x) or exact (3.47.4), same semantics as subosito/flutter-action'
    required: true

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Resolve pin and reuse-or-install the SDK
      id: sdk
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail

        SPEC='${{ inputs.flutter-version }}'
        SDK_ROOT="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk"
        CURRENT="$SDK_ROOT/current"   # symlink -> $SDK_ROOT/<version>
        MARKER="$SDK_ROOT/.fah-version"
        SLOT="${{ github.action_path }}/sdk_slot.py"
        mkdir -p "$SDK_ROOT"

        # Pre-#357 layouts kept the live SDK in a real `current`
        # directory — move it into its per-version slot once,
        # race-tolerantly (a concurrent leg that loses the migration
        # no-ops; os.rename never merges).
        python3 "$SLOT" migrate "$SDK_ROOT" "$MARKER"

        # Resolve the spec to a concrete stable version from the
        # official manifest (same resolution subosito/flutter-action
        # performs), then decide: SKIP (marker == wanted), REUSE
        # (manifest unreachable but the pinned SDK still satisfies the
        # spec) or INSTALL. The committed scenarios live in
        # test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart.
        DECISION="$(python3 "$SLOT" resolve "$SPEC" "$MARKER")"
        echo "$DECISION"
        VER="${DECISION#* }"
        DEST="$SDK_ROOT/$VER"

        # Self-heal before trusting a non-INSTALL verdict: a marker can
        # point at a version dir that a human or disk cleanup removed.
        # Without this the SKIP path would export a PATH entry with no
        # flutter binary under it and every later step would die at
        # `flutter --version` until someone deletes the marker by hand —
        # the brick the #357 review flagged on the old swap.
        if [[ "$DECISION" != INSTALL* && ! -d "$DEST" ]]; then
          echo "pinned $VER is missing from $SDK_ROOT — reinstalling"
          DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
        fi

        if [[ "$DECISION" == INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "Flutter $VER already installed by a concurrent leg — reusing it"
          else
            echo "Downloading Flutter $VER (spec: $SPEC) — one-time per pinned version..."
            STAGE="$(mktemp -d "$SDK_ROOT/.stage.XXXXXX")"
            # --max-time bounds EACH transfer, --retry-max-time bounds
            # the whole retry cycle: a wedged ~1GB download can never
            # hang the job until GitHub's ceiling kills it. (Same
            # pattern as the bounded asset downloads in build-macos.)
            if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
                --max-time 600 --retry-max-time 900 \
                -o "$STAGE/flutter.zip" \
                "https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/releases/stable/macos/flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip"; then
              echo "::error::Flutter SDK download for $VER failed after retries (bounded: --max-time 600 per attempt, --retry-max-time 900 total). The runner's network or storage.googleapis.com is unhealthy — check and re-run; partial state stayed inside $STAGE only, the pinned slot is untouched."
              exit 1
            fi
            unzip -q "$STAGE/flutter.zip" -d "$STAGE"
            # Atomic slot-in: rename(2) either lands the complete tree
            # or refuses because a concurrent leg already installed the
            # identical version — the loser discards its duplicate
            # (both legs fetch the same archive, so the bytes match).
            python3 "$SLOT" install "$STAGE/flutter" "$DEST"
            rm -rf "$STAGE"
          fi
        elif [[ "$DECISION" == REUSE* ]]; then
          echo "::warning::Flutter manifest unreachable — reusing pinned SDK $VER (satisfies $SPEC)"
        else
          echo "Flutter $VER already pinned at $CURRENT — skipping the download (issue #354)"
        fi

        # Publish the slot with one atomic symlink swap — idempotent
        # under concurrency (both matrix legs flip to the same target).
        # Readers resolve `current` per use, so they observe either the
        # previous complete tree or this one, never a missing or
        # half-populated SDK; superseded trees are only gc'd after a
        # 2-day drain window, so in-flight legs keep a complete tree.
        python3 "$SLOT" flip "$DEST" "$CURRENT"
        echo "$VER" > "$MARKER"
        echo "Pinned Flutter $VER at $CURRENT -> $DEST"
        python3 "$SLOT" gc "$SDK_ROOT" "$DEST" 2

        # No actions/cache anywhere in this path: there is no POST step,
        # so no re-tar of the ~1GB SDK after every job.
        echo "$CURRENT/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        echo "FLUTTER_ROOT=$CURRENT" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        "$CURRENT/bin/flutter" --version

binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, supply-chain, dep-audit]
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || fail "changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || fail "supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || fail "dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          # The remaining legs are path-gated: success or skipped is fine,
          # anything else fails.
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
              fail "a leg is $r ($name)"
            fi
          done
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      (github.event.inputs.pr != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, mirroring the pinned factory's own block
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write). A reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the caller, so the
# caller must grant at least what the callee declares — an explicit
# read-only block here made every call fail validation with
# startup_failure (live bisect, 2026-09-18); this mirror is the minimal
# consistent set (SEC-08, #796).
permissions:
  contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
  issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
  actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
    # The workflow-level mirror scopes exist for the pinned factory call
    # (a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller); the gate
    # must not inherit them (SEC-08 review, #796).
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 849
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/849
- **Title**: feat(ci): SHA-pinned actions + pin-freshness automation (#796)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-796` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 20
- **Additions**: +520
- **Deletions**: -232
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T20:31:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-23T00:57:20Z

## PR Description

Supersedes #801 (owner-closed unmerged over a merge conflict; reopen refused for non-owner). Same branch `ai/gh-796`, now rebased onto main @ 10715955 (carries #846 runner split, #847 factory pin 54e86fd, #848 SM-gate-bridge). Closes #796 (SEC-08, HIGH).

## What
1. **Every third-party Actions ref in `.github/workflows/*.yml` + composite actions is a full 40-hex commit SHA** (213 refs, 13 distinct actions; SHAs resolved via the GitHub API at pin time). First-party repo-relative refs stay exempt. The factory `uses:` lines (machine-sm.yml, ai-teammate.yml, machine-merge.yml) keep main's current pins (54e86fd) — only the surrounding permissions blocks were added.
2. **Every workflow declares an explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` block** (caller⇄reusable consistent). The ai-teammate mirror is exactly the pinned factory's declared scopes (contents/issues/pull-requests/actions = write — an explicit read-only caller block startup_failure'd the reusable call; live bisect 2026-09-18). The read-only `gate` job narrows further to `contents: read`.
3. **Dual-graph dependency audit**: `dep-audit` matrix [hosted, vendored] — hosted = `pubspec.yaml` alone (what pub.dev consumers resolve), vendored = + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` (CI/release). The split is asserted from the resolved `pubspec.lock` (dart_tui `source: hosted` vs `source: path`), anchored to the entry block boundary, and documented in each leg's job summary.
4. **Supply-chain gate on every PR** (no path gating): AC1 pin-check script (`scripts/check_action_pins.sh` — refs must match `\^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$`; composite actions scanned depth-unlimited, both extensions), AC2 permissions lint (*.yml + *.yaml), AC4 fixture REG (@v4, 40-char non-hex, unpinned nested composite all REJECTED; SHA-pinned accepted).
5. **Quality gate hardening**: a failed/skipped `changes` classifier FAILS the aggregate, and the security legs (supply-chain, dep-audit) must EXECUTE and pass — `skipped` is a dodge, not a pass. Path-gated legs keep success|skipped semantics.
6. **Pin freshness (contract)**: `.github/dependabot.yml` — github-actions ecosystem, weekly, grouped into one PR; Dependabot bumps SHA-pinned refs and their `# vX` comments.

# pr-849: feat(ci): SHA-pinned actions + pin-freshness automation (#796)

## Description

Supersedes #801 (owner-closed unmerged over a merge conflict; reopen refused for non-owner). Same branch `ai/gh-796`, now rebased onto main @ 10715955 (carries #846 runner split, #847 factory pin 54e86fd, #848 SM-gate-bridge). Closes #796 (SEC-08, HIGH).

## What
1. **Every third-party Actions ref in `.github/workflows/*.yml` + composite actions is a full 40-hex commit SHA** (213 refs, 13 distinct actions; SHAs resolved via the GitHub API at pin time). First-party repo-relative refs stay exempt. The factory `uses:` lines (machine-sm.yml, ai-teammate.yml, machine-merge.yml) keep main's current pins (54e86fd) — only the surrounding permissions blocks were added.
2. **Every workflow declares an explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` block** (caller⇄reusable consistent). The ai-teammate mirror is exactly the pinned factory's declared scopes (contents/issues/pull-requests/actions = write — an explicit read-only caller block startup_failure'd the reusable call; live bisect 2026-09-18). The read-only `gate` job narrows further to `contents: read`.
3. **Dual-graph dependency audit**: `dep-audit` matrix [hosted, vendored] — hosted = `pubspec.yaml` alone (what pub.dev consumers resolve), vendored = + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` (CI/release). The split is asserted from the resolved `pubspec.lock` (dart_tui `source: hosted` vs `source: path`), anchored to the entry block boundary, and documented in each leg's job summary.
4. **Supply-chain gate on every PR** (no path gating): AC1 pin-check script (`scripts/check_action_pins.sh` — refs must match `\^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$`; composite actions scanned depth-unlimited, both extensions), AC2 permissions lint (*.yml + *.yaml), AC4 fixture REG (@v4, 40-char non-hex, unpinned nested composite all REJECTED; SHA-pinned accepted).
5. **Quality gate hardening**: a failed/skipped `changes` classifier FAILS the aggregate, and the security legs (supply-chain, dep-audit) must EXECUTE and pass — `skipped` is a dodge, not a pass. Path-gated legs keep success|skipped semantics.
6. **Pin freshness (contract)**: `.github/dependabot.yml` — github-actions ecosystem, weekly, grouped into one PR; Dependabot bumps SHA-pinned refs and their `# vX` comments.

## Coexistence with #848
#848 exempts `chore:pin` PRs from the SM gate bridge; this PR's pin checker still runs on every other PR and over #848's own content (verified: scan passes on the merged tree).

- ruby/setup-ruby pinned at the v1.99.0 release-tag commit `e5517072e87f198d9533967ae13d97c11b604005` (ls-remote verified), 7 call sites in lockstep.

- Dependabot's first weekly run will open the grouped bump PR; the supply-chain gate re-verifies every ref on it.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved

  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

---
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
